title: Host has no sub-second, dated timestamps for turn, queue and approval boundaries, so latency can't be attributed
outcome: Every turn, queue, approval and command boundary carries a dated, millisecond, clock-aligned timestamp that an external disk sampler can line up with its own readings.
acceptance: Each boundary listed in the notes (arrival, queue entry and dequeue, approval/elicitation creation and resolution, Codex turn/start dispatch and turn/started, turn end, command start and end) carries an RFC3339 UTC timestamp with at least millisecond precision and a monotonic offset relative to a per-start anchor, both readable through a documented read-only endpoint.
The per-start anchor (UTC time and monotonic origin) is exported together with serverInstanceId, so an external sampler can align the host's monotonic offsets to its own clock.
Existing display timestamps and their wire format are unchanged; cargo test --bin termal is green, with tests covering a queued turn, an approval resolved after a delay, and a completed command.
